BiblicalUsage: Arnan is named once, in the line of David, as a son of Rephaiah, and the chronicler gives his name and his brothers and nothing more. He stands in the genealogy between the exile and the return.
TheologicalSignificance: A name in a genealogy with no story of its own still matters, because God keeps the line of David name by name, even through the generations nobody writes about.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
